Queenstown: Komani: A Town in Crises

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Queenstown municipality has auctioned off it's vehicles to pay for a historical debt, but the municipality is in tatters, and there is no water, electricity of service delivery.

Unique Selling Point:
GOING, GOING, GONE: Various municipal vehicles, most of which are imperative for service deliverywere sold today at an auction to recover millions of rands owed by the Enoch Mgijima Local Municipalityto Milowo Trading Enterprise. Robert Goss of Milowo Trading Enterprise said he and his legal representatives would soon file for municipal buildings to be sold as well. The debt owed to Milowo trading, following the building of a community hall in Sterkstroom in 2012, and accumulated interest, has been set at R58-million. Vehicles that went under the hammer included 18 trucks, various traffic vehicles and a grader. The full story will be in The Rep next week Picture: ANDISA BONANI
It was decided that the town would go under section 123 (That’s under administration) – but they haven’t decided whether that’s division a,b,c yet. However, they still might go under section 125, because they are saying that treasury’s R100 million was not enough to assist them during the amalgamation. (The municipality amalgamated late last year – from 3 to 1). But it needs to be properly approved. Then they are going to have a SECOND auction because they didn’t make enough on the first, but they want to have a meeting about it before – it’s meant to go ahead on July 29th.
Their current Mayor and Municipal Manager were only appointed in February. The manager was embroiled in the 600 million toilet Mandela scandal, and there are rumours about the Mayors BMW. We will do a full audit on both of them and their families, the community know a lot about where they live etc.


Summary:
Information on:Queenstown Enoch Mgijima Local Municipality, District Municipality is Chris Hani: The number of inhabitants in Enoch Mgijima LM is 245,975. This is 3.3% of the total population in the province Eastern Cape. The Local Municipality with the largest population in the province Eastern Cape is King Sabata Dalindyebo with 451,711 inhabitants (9.7%). The boundaries of the three former local municipalities have been re-determined and a new demarcation map with the new wards is the following: The total population, after the re-determination of the boundaries in 2016 is approximately 245,975. The following is a summary of key datasets for Enoch Mgijima Municipality.

Further information:
CONFRONTS:
Interview with Mayor - Ms. Nokuzola Sisisi Tolashe
Interview with Manager - Chris Magwangqana
Interview with Adré Bartis - Border-Kei Chamber of Business - they are an NGO and are responsible for representing business in the town of komani/ queenstown.
She would talk about the following:
Service delivery protest has been our entertainment over the last 3 weeks which also included the burning down of a community hall, school and EPWP centre in the communities. It might sound as if the community is just being petty and not understanding the value of what they have, however a closer look at what they have to go through might shed some light on their frustrations (please note I am not condoning their behaviours at all).
In January we had both our main substations hit by lightning and our transformers were blown. After that no maintenance or replacements were done and only one of the transformers were fixed. The town was struggling on almost a weekly basis after that with either cables or subs blowing and affecting most of the Business areas.
June has been a crazy month: 5th June - A breaker in the Queens Industria tripping the transformer in Ebden Street, providing a total blackout of 12 hours to the town.
6th June the transformer in Ebden came on for 20 minutes and exploded bringing the town to total darkness for 23 hours. This would have been longer but a team was called from EL to assist. They also requested parts from Buffalo City metro to fix the issue. They used the new transformer that has been standing for the last 3 years and this was electrified for the first time in 3 years.
15 June the breaker in Ezibeleni went again and assured 45% of the town without electricity for 3 days. Although the District Municipality made provision for water through generators it seems like this is only being used if the whole town is affected because the 45% was not provided with water for the entire duration of their electricity failure.
27 June – the transformer in the Queens Industria blacked out with no reason provided and left the factory areas without electricity for 6 hours. Sporadic bursts of electricity followed for 2 days after that.
29 June the transformer blacked out for no reason and it shut down 80% of the town. 4 Hours later 40% of the 80% has been restored and 8 hours later another 10%. The rest came on 17 hours later.
30 June Queen Industria, Aloe Vale, New vale, Ezibeleni Zone 1 and 4 was switched of due to low voltage and have been of until today with no communication from the municipalities to these areas.
Today 3 July – The transformer in Wainwright Street burnt out affecting 6 streets including the Private Hospital and the Casino. This has not been restored as yet and the areas are also left without water. These are all the issues we struggle with on a daily basis that no one budgeted for and that leaves business and the people they employ in total frustration. This is only on electricity and not on all the other infrastructure issues which is also in a state of emergency.
So what has the Chamber done to assist with this debacle? The January crisis had the local office running to site every day, 6 times daily to provide updates vie Whatsapp and Facebook platforms to ensure current information was being given. This ran for 5 days nonstop with some updates being given as early as 2am in the morning. The Director (Les Holbrook) was informing platforms such as ECSECC of the current situation in Queenstown and made personal contact with the Premier’s office. This followed by the Director, the than Chairman (Adré Bartis) and a member of Chamber (Ken Clark) to attend 4 meetings with the Premier, MEC of COGTA, ECSECC, Provincial Treasury, the Local and District Municipality. The Director had ongoing contact it ECSESS and COGTA and the local Chair had to sit in on meetings at the Local Municipal level. This also meant attending each Council meeting to ensure that all necessary information was received to assist with the intervention. Another meeting was attended by Ken and Adré to try and stop the auction that was held because of a R44m debt incurred for a community hall that was built in Sterkstroom but this was unfortunately out of their hands as the final decision lay with the MM of EMLM. Adré also met with a team where the MEC of COGTA was providing an update of the issues and what they as COGTA will be committing too.
Fixing the issues at hand is not going to be an easy overnight task, especially when you have the 2 municipalities not really communicating with each other and electrical issues alone sitting on R100m before we can see any transformation in this town. EMLM has Komani, Sterkstroom, Ilinge, Lesseyton, Molteno, Tarkastad, Hoffmeyer, Tsolwana game reserve and all the rural areas to service. Currently they have 4 bakkies, 1 truck and 1 Cherry Picker to do the work in all these areas. This is for the technical department only. Unless they get a big cash injection and teams to support all the departments, we will be sitting with this problem for a while. But not all is dark, we continue to fight and get to work with everyone that is willing to assist this Municipality where we are and always have been willing to roll our sleeves up.

Interview with Rep journalists – Mr. Mgidi and Ms. Bonani and their editor has information on the schools.
Tell us about the protests and provide footage
Take us to residents and potential sources
Chat to daily dispatch – Mr. Zolilwe Menzelwe 063 369 9557 (he’s in east London)
Won an award for her investigation on Magwangqana – on the R600 million toilet scandal. He was head of SALGA, his initial appointment was rescinded at Enoch Municipality, but then given back to him. Hawks were assigned to investigate him by treasury but nothing has happened since.
Principal at local government high school Southbourne – Marelise Bekker 0827761811
She has sent me a lot more information – it’s actually effecting many of the schools in the area. It’s a shocker – the contractor wasn’t paid, and now they are sitting without classrooms.
– she wants to speak anonymously about the school – otherwise she’ll be fired. She has the footage ready for us and others that can speak.
DA councilor Chris de Wet 0828718091
He has lots of information says he has insiders – I will go through everything with him.

Queenstown Civic and Ratepayers' Association chairman Tokkie Daysel – accounts dispute. No accounts, incorrect information, incorrect billing – 083 452 7115.
Local businessman: Ken Clarke – owner of dairy farm – 200 ppl – business effected with water and electricity cuts – they are a massive industry for the town 082 558 9939
I also have the contact details for the ward counselor who was responsible for the municipality – apparently he is on the side of the residents – But I will only call him once I have the other information and have met with Adre from Commerce Chamber.

Press Release:


Komani’s Municipal Meltdown
No water or electricity, millions of rands of debt and auctioning off its municipal assets, Komani’s Enoch Mgijima municipality is in crisis and unable to provide basic services. Despite selling off a fire engine, road graders and garbage collection trucks, the municipality still owes millions. Residents are fed up, demanding that their troubled town is placed under administration. Carte Blanche tracks this developing story.


Script:


Video Audio
Children playing in trash - stabilize
- show overflowing toilet

ON SCREEN: Mlungisi
Drone - ring traffic light
Examples of non-service delivery You’d be forgiven for thinking Mlungisi township in the Eastern Cape is a rubbish dump: Children play around overflowing toilets. No electricity. No drinking water when there’s a blackout. Sewage in the streets.
In town, things are not much better. Broken traffic lights. Potholes. No street lights.
How did THIS town fall into such a severe state of disrepair?
Derek Link
on screen: R26 million LINK: MORE THAN HALF THEIR INCOME SPENT ON SALARIES, 26 MILLION ON BANK CHARGES, NO ACCOUNTING SYSTEM, THE AUDITOR GENERAL COULDN’T DO HIS JOB BECAUSE THERE WERE NO DOCUMENTS, NOT EVEN BANK STATEMENTS. WELCOME TO QUEENSTOWN, NOW KNOWN AS KOMANI.
Drone
Historical visuals.

STRAP: Date 1985 Famous for the 1985 protests against atrocious living conditions, this region was ironically the heartland of the ANC’s political activism...33 years later, there’s again outrage as residents say they’re forgotten and neglected.
PEOPLE LIGHTING TYRES
Courtesy: The Rep and Tiso Blackstar Community Newspapers. UPSOUND: FIRE BURNING
Mlungisi – rep visuals -
STRAP: Date June Last month Mlungisi residents protested. Journalist Simtembile Mgidi reports for The Rep, one of the country’s oldest community newspapers .
UPSOUND: SCREAMING PROTESTORS
Rep journo - Simtembile Mgidi
Simtembile: “During the protest march you could not go through this street.”

ON SCREEN: Ezibileni


picture of nokuzola In neighbouring Ezibeleni violence erupted and looting broke out. The Rep’s Andisa Bonani saw protestors set fire to buildings to send the message that newly appointed Mayor Noku-zola Tolashe was not welcome.
Bonani Bonani: “It’s a newly built hall, which cost the municipality lots of money to build for the community members.”
Protes visuals from rep Upsound: Protestors
Komani City protests - rep

#140 million to fix town’s grid on screen From across suburbs, residents were united in their anger over the constant power outages. According to councilor Chris de Wet, it will cost R140 million to repair the town’s grid.
By power grid Chris de Wet: “During the course of last month, this transformer literally exploded, our whole grid is overloaded, the electric network of this town has not been maintained for over 15 years.”
Drone komani at night At night Komani city is in darkness.
Chris - ADD DEREK reversal Chris: “A lot of the street lights that are not working, I’ve tried talking to the technical department about fixing them, we do not have one street light bulb in our store to fix the light.”
Cherry picker (zoom) - ring wheels
But even if they could fix the lights the cherry picker has no wheels.
Derek LINK: THE LACK OF SERVICE DELIVERY, ALONG WITH WATER AND POWER CUTS HAS MADE LIFE VERY DIFFICULT FOR THE KOMANI COMMUNITY, BUT WHEN YOU TALK RANDS AND CENTS THE CORPORATE SECTOR HAS ALSO TAKEN A HUGE KNOCK.
Ken Clark KEN CLARK: “THE ELECTRICAL SITUATION IN THIS TOWN CAN BE LIKENED TO A PATIENT WHO IS IN THE OPERATING THEATRE IN SURGERY AND THE SURGEONS WALKS AWAY.”
Businesses affected - change shot
On screen: R200,000 loss Ken Clark employs roughly 500 people at his dairy and soft drink factories. Power cuts cost him R200,000 a day .
Ken Clark


Ken: “The municipality was losing money to the tune of R10 million per month...under such conditions, obviously you’re going to start falling behind in payments – we are now R85 million behind with payments to Eskom.”
Kids burning trash

translate


These orphaned teenagers collect scrap metal for R20-R50 a day to survive.
Sim: “So you are taking care of your family? So you’re a breadwinner by default.”
They blame the townships 80% unemployment rate on mismanagement by Enoch Mgijima Local Municipality, that’s resulted in few job opportunities.
Tokkie Deysel intro

43# on screen Queenstown Civic and Ratepayers Association chairman Tokkie Deysel says Enoch Mgijima under-collected by R43 million last year.
Tokkie Tokkie Daysel: “I want to quote the municipal systems act, it says you must take reasonable steps to make sure that users of services are informed of the costs involved in services provision.”
Derek: “What is happening with residents rates bills?”
Tokkie: “The last time we received a bills was in December of last year. If you don’t receive a bill, what would an ordinary person do?”
Video AG report



Amalgamation - map 4:00 Because there were no documents like payslips, bank statements or even an accounting system, the Auditor General -- damningly -- couldn’t express an audit opinion on the state of their financials.
The municipality merged with two smaller towns in 2015 - which enlarged municipal boundaries and increased the service delivery burden. Adre Bartis, Chairperson of the Border-Kei Chamber of Business says the decline began after its amalgamation.
Amalgamation - adre Adre Bartis: “The municipality has really been struggling, didn’t get the money to see them into it, they didn’t get the admin support, and if .you don’t get any of that, you can’t just take a child, throw them in the river and expect them to swim.”
Name: Chris Magwangqana
Courtesy: The Daily Dispatch and Tiso Blackstar
see more of the town… context...


red line…
ON SCREEN: R90,000
(freeze)
and then a beat before derek In January Chris Magwangqana became Municipal Manager, a post he’d also held at Amathola municipality where he was embroiled in a R630-million toilet scandal…66000 toilets were planned but few materialised. An audit report recommended he face criminal and disciplinary action. The Hawks are investigating and Magwangqana denied any wrongdoing saying it was no more than a political vendetta against him. Within days of his appointment, financial show that R90,000 was spent on fried chicken roughly 2500 colonel burgers.
Derek link
on screen: R14 million
LINK: IT’S NOT A PLEASANT SITE OR SMELL...LITTER EVERYWHERE, AND IT’S PART OF A R14 MILLION PROJECT ironically CALLED THE BEAUTIFICATION OF KOMANI RIVER.
Intro Zuko Taxi rank visual
#30 million Councilor Zuko Mandisa, says money is poured into unfinished projects. Some never open --like this R30 million taxi rank.
Zuko intv Zuko: “The whole of South africa, no one is held accountable, it’s been proven by the auditor general and no one is taken to book.”
Derek LINK: SO WHAT DO YOU DO WHEN YOU CAN’T DELIVER ON BASIC SERVICES AND YOUR COMMUNITY IS PROTESTING IN THE STREETS. WELL, IT MAY SOUND UNBELIEVABLE, BUT YOU HOLD AND AUCTION OF ESSENTIAL VEHICLES AND EQUIPMENT.
Upsound: “Auctioneer: Going once for R250,000, going twice…”
Date: July
Auction - on screen: #44 vehicles
Courtesy: The Rep and Tiso Blackstar Community Newspapers.


Document - make nice
name Nokuzola Tolashe 44 vehicles -- garbage trucks, ambulances and fire trucks went under the hammer to settle a R21 million debt. Assets were sold for half their value and raised less than a third of what was needed - therefore a second auction was advertised for later this month. The ANC seconded Mayor Nokuzola Tolashe. The Municipal Manager announced that a multi-party committee would investigate the auction. The day before our interview, they said they’d paid Eskom, and had a rescue plan.
Mayor intv
IMAGES BACK - SAD COW Derek: “How do you rate your score card since taking over as Mayor?”
Mayor Tolashe: “If you said the total is 10, I would say 8.”
wide It seems she doesn’t grasp the gravity of the situation.
Mayor Derek: “How do you react to seeing skulls and bones piled up at the Komani river, rubbish littered everywhere and children playing in sewage.”
Mayor: “It’s very bad, it’s very pathetic. One of the things we committed in our budget for this financial year, is that we address that.”
Show truck going past We told her about the lack of rubbish collection.
Simtembile Simtembile: “They just drove past and forgot the rubbish bags and dead dog. It will sit here for months.”
Mayor intv Mayor: “Sometimes, it’s not being collected sometimes, sometimes because our trucks could not really afford that.”
Mayor intv Derek: “But now how can you clean up the streets and solve the situation when you’ve sold equipment on auction?”
Mayor: “Not, because we had a choice. We are still contesting that we don’t owe those people.”
derek wide Chris: “Unfortunately on the day, neither the mayor nor the speaker could be contacted, they were just not available.”
Mayor Mayor: “I was always part of the team that was trying to avoid the situation, it was so unfortunate.”
Document over auction It was only when municipal assets were attached by the sheriff last month that the public – and even the councilors -- became aware of the impending auction. De Wet says the municipality didn’t even defend the judgment.
Chris: “We as counselors get only informed what they want us to know, that is why we didn’t know that the company that sold all our assets took judgment against us already in March.”
Derek: “You had multiple opportunities to stop the auction, and you knew about it since January?”
MM: “In January there was a summons, and it was taken to the lawyers, and what else should a MM in between done?”
Municipal Manager The municipal manager says there will be no second auction as the debt has now been settled. He admitted the amalgamation process failed.
Amalgamation MM: “Amalgamation as it is now, we could write a thesis about amalgamation of Enoch Mgijima, of what has not been properly done.”
Derek: “Is that an excuse?”
MM: “It is something that we have not been able to master as a country.”
Derek: “So is that why you’re under-collecting to the tune of 10’s of millions?”
MM: “Do you know currently what our collection rate is? I’ll tell you, it’s just around 70%.”
Tokkie Deysel Tokkie: “70% of what? Is it 70% of what they billed? And who did they bill?”
We were assured an accounting system is now in place.
MM: “Ask in me in November about my own audit results. You will see a difference.”
Derek: “So it’s not going to be even worse picture.”
MM: “No it can’t be, it can’t be worse I guarantee you.”
But will money be spent on delivering services? Some say not, as it was reported the municipality spent R300,000 on a mayoral public relations event.
Derek: “I see a conflict between the skulls, bones fences at Komani and spending on thousands at a mayoral address, apparently R300,000?”
Mayor: “Whatever figure that you might put, but for us to bring back the trust of the community, but also to make them understand what the government is doing for them, especially this fee of government, you have to spend money.”
Rental car mayor Derek: “It was reported that you are driving a rental car which is costing R78,000 a month, is that true?”
Mayor: “That is for one reason, is that the car driven by the former mayor is in repairs.”
But the mayoral car has been in repairs for half a year.
Rental car MM

volvo pictures MM: “Let’s say yes, it comes to that amount.”
Derek: “But that is just incredible? I don’t know what you spend R78,000 on. It’s a Volvo?”
MM: “Unless you’re saying we were given a raw deal?”
Fried Chicken MM Derek: “On your list of priorities is it more important to spend R90,000 on fried chicken or money on cleaning up the townships.”
MM: “The priorities of this mun has been sent is the roads, electricity, cleanliness of the city.”
Derek: “But you haven’t answered the question.”
MM: “If you compare to what we spend to cleaning up the towns and township each month, that R90,000 is far less.”
Derek: “Madam mayor at Carte Blanche we are used to people making promises.”
Mayor: “Please do come back in 6 months. The future is very bright for this municipality.”
One certainty is that the stench of maladministration across many of South Africa’s municipality’s needs to be cleaned up – just like Komani’s streets.

Komani’s Municipal Meltdown No water or electricity, millions of rands of debt and auctioning off its municipal assets, Komani’s Enoch Mgijima municipality is in crisis and unable to provide basic services. Despite selling off a fire engine, road graders and garbage collection trucks, the municipality still owes millions. Residents are fed up, demanding that their troubled town is placed under administration. Carte Blanche tracks this developing story. Script: Video Audio Children playing in trash - stabilize - show overflowing toilet ON SCREEN: Mlungisi Drone - ring traffic light Examples of non-service delivery You’d be forgiven for thinking Mlungisi township in the Eastern Cape is a rubbish dump: Children play around overflowing toilets. No electricity. No drinking water when there’s a blackout. Sewage in the streets. In town, things are not much better. Broken traffic lights. Potholes. No street lights. How did THIS town fall into such a severe state of disrepair? Derek Link on screen: R26 million LINK: MORE THAN HALF THEIR INCOME SPENT ON SALARIES, 26 MILLION ON BANK CHARGES, NO ACCOUNTING SYSTEM, THE AUDITOR GENERAL COULDN’T DO HIS JOB BECAUSE THERE WERE NO DOCUMENTS, NOT EVEN BANK STATEMENTS. WELCOME TO QUEENSTOWN, NOW KNOWN AS KOMANI. Drone Historical visuals. STRAP: Date 1985 Famous for the 1985 protests against atrocious living conditions, this region was ironically the heartland of the ANC’s political activism...33 years later, there’s again outrage as residents say they’re forgotten and neglected. PEOPLE LIGHTING TYRES Courtesy: The Rep and Tiso Blackstar Community Newspapers. UPSOUND: FIRE BURNING Mlungisi – rep visuals - STRAP: Date June Last month Mlungisi residents protested. Journalist Simtembile Mgidi reports for The Rep, one of the country’s oldest community newspapers . UPSOUND: SCREAMING PROTESTORS Rep journo - Simtembile Mgidi Simtembile: “During the protest march you could not go through this street.” ON SCREEN: Ezibileni picture of nokuzola In neighbouring Ezibeleni violence erupted and looting broke out. The Rep’s Andisa Bonani saw protestors set fire to buildings to send the message that newly appointed Mayor Noku-zola Tolashe was not welcome. Bonani Bonani: “It’s a newly built hall, which cost the municipality lots of money to build for the community members.” Protes visuals from rep Upsound: Protestors Komani City protests - rep #140 million to fix town’s grid on screen From across suburbs, residents were united in their anger over the constant power outages. According to councilor Chris de Wet, it will cost R140 million to repair the town’s grid. By power grid Chris de Wet: “During the course of last month, this transformer literally exploded, our whole grid is overloaded, the electric network of this town has not been maintained for over 15 years.” Drone komani at night At night Komani city is in darkness. Chris - ADD DEREK reversal Chris: “A lot of the street lights that are not working, I’ve tried talking to the technical department about fixing them, we do not have one street light bulb in our store to fix the light.” Cherry picker (zoom) - ring wheels But even if they could fix the lights the cherry picker has no wheels. Derek LINK: THE LACK OF SERVICE DELIVERY, ALONG WITH WATER AND POWER CUTS HAS MADE LIFE VERY DIFFICULT FOR THE KOMANI COMMUNITY, BUT WHEN YOU TALK RANDS AND CENTS THE CORPORATE SECTOR HAS ALSO TAKEN A HUGE KNOCK. Ken Clark KEN CLARK: “THE ELECTRICAL SITUATION IN THIS TOWN CAN BE LIKENED TO A PATIENT WHO IS IN THE OPERATING THEATRE IN SURGERY AND THE SURGEONS WALKS AWAY.” Businesses affected - change shot On screen: R200,000 loss Ken Clark employs roughly 500 people at his dairy and soft drink factories. Power cuts cost him R200,000 a day . Ken Clark Ken: “The municipality was losing money to the tune of R10 million per month...under such conditions, obviously you’re going to start falling behind in payments – we are now R85 million behind with payments to Eskom.” Kids burning trash translate These orphaned teenagers collect scrap metal for R20-R50 a day to survive. Sim: “So you are taking care of your family? So you’re a breadwinner by default.” They blame the townships 80% unemployment rate on mismanagement by Enoch Mgijima Local Municipality, that’s resulted in few job opportunities. Tokkie Deysel intro 43# on screen Queenstown Civic and Ratepayers Association chairman Tokkie Deysel says Enoch Mgijima under-collected by R43 million last year. Tokkie Tokkie Daysel: “I want to quote the municipal systems act, it says you must take reasonable steps to make sure that users of services are informed of the costs involved in services provision.” Derek: “What is happening with residents rates bills?” Tokkie: “The last time we received a bills was in December of last year. If you don’t receive a bill, what would an ordinary person do?” Video AG report Amalgamation - map 4:00 Because there were no documents like payslips, bank statements or even an accounting system, the Auditor General -- damningly -- couldn’t express an audit opinion on the state of their financials. The municipality merged with two smaller towns in 2015 - which enlarged municipal boundaries and increased the service delivery burden. Adre Bartis, Chairperson of the Border-Kei Chamber of Business says the decline began after its amalgamation. Amalgamation - adre Adre Bartis: “The municipality has really been struggling, didn’t get the money to see them into it, they didn’t get the admin support, and if .you don’t get any of that, you can’t just take a child, throw them in the river and expect them to swim.” Name: Chris Magwangqana Courtesy: The Daily Dispatch and Tiso Blackstar see more of the town… context... red line… ON SCREEN: R90,000 (freeze) and then a beat before derek In January Chris Magwangqana became Municipal Manager, a post he’d also held at Amathola municipality where he was embroiled in a R630-million toilet scandal…66000 toilets were planned but few materialised. An audit report recommended he face criminal and disciplinary action. The Hawks are investigating and Magwangqana denied any wrongdoing saying it was no more than a political vendetta against him. Within days of his appointment, financial show that R90,000 was spent on fried chicken roughly 2500 colonel burgers. Derek link on screen: R14 million LINK: IT’S NOT A PLEASANT SITE OR SMELL...LITTER EVERYWHERE, AND IT’S PART OF A R14 MILLION PROJECT ironically CALLED THE BEAUTIFICATION OF KOMANI RIVER. Intro Zuko Taxi rank visual #30 million Councilor Zuko Mandisa, says money is poured into unfinished projects. Some never open --like this R30 million taxi rank. Zuko intv Zuko: “The whole of South africa, no one is held accountable, it’s been proven by the auditor general and no one is taken to book.” Derek LINK: SO WHAT DO YOU DO WHEN YOU CAN’T DELIVER ON BASIC SERVICES AND YOUR COMMUNITY IS PROTESTING IN THE STREETS. WELL, IT MAY SOUND UNBELIEVABLE, BUT YOU HOLD AND AUCTION OF ESSENTIAL VEHICLES AND EQUIPMENT. Upsound: “Auctioneer: Going once for R250,000, going twice…” Date: July Auction - on screen: #44 vehicles Courtesy: The Rep and Tiso Blackstar Community Newspapers. Document - make nice name Nokuzola Tolashe 44 vehicles -- garbage trucks, ambulances and fire trucks went under the hammer to settle a R21 million debt. Assets were sold for half their value and raised less than a third of what was needed - therefore a second auction was advertised for later this month. The ANC seconded Mayor Nokuzola Tolashe. The Municipal Manager announced that a multi-party committee would investigate the auction. The day before our interview, they said they’d paid Eskom, and had a rescue plan. Mayor intv IMAGES BACK - SAD COW Derek: “How do you rate your score card since taking over as Mayor?” Mayor Tolashe: “If you said the total is 10, I would say 8.” wide It seems she doesn’t grasp the gravity of the situation. Mayor Derek: “How do you react to seeing skulls and bones piled up at the Komani river, rubbish littered everywhere and children playing in sewage.” Mayor: “It’s very bad, it’s very pathetic. One of the things we committed in our budget for this financial year, is that we address that.” Show truck going past We told her about the lack of rubbish collection. Simtembile Simtembile: “They just drove past and forgot the rubbish bags and dead dog. It will sit here for months.” Mayor intv Mayor: “Sometimes, it’s not being collected sometimes, sometimes because our trucks could not really afford that.” Mayor intv Derek: “But now how can you clean up the streets and solve the situation when you’ve sold equipment on auction?” Mayor: “Not, because we had a choice. We are still contesting that we don’t owe those people.” derek wide Chris: “Unfortunately on the day, neither the mayor nor the speaker could be contacted, they were just not available.” Mayor Mayor: “I was always part of the team that was trying to avoid the situation, it was so unfortunate.” Document over auction It was only when municipal assets were attached by the sheriff last month that the public – and even the councilors -- became aware of the impending auction. De Wet says the municipality didn’t even defend the judgment. Chris: “We as counselors get only informed what they want us to know, that is why we didn’t know that the company that sold all our assets took judgment against us already in March.” Derek: “You had multiple opportunities to stop the auction, and you knew about it since January?” MM: “In January there was a summons, and it was taken to the lawyers, and what else should a MM in between done?” Municipal Manager The municipal manager says there will be no second auction as the debt has now been settled. He admitted the amalgamation process failed. Amalgamation MM: “Amalgamation as it is now, we could write a thesis about amalgamation of Enoch Mgijima, of what has not been properly done.” Derek: “Is that an excuse?” MM: “It is something that we have not been able to master as a country.” Derek: “So is that why you’re under-collecting to the tune of 10’s of millions?” MM: “Do you know currently what our collection rate is? I’ll tell you, it’s just around 70%.” Tokkie Deysel Tokkie: “70% of what? Is it 70% of what they billed? And who did they bill?” We were assured an accounting system is now in place. MM: “Ask in me in November about my own audit results. You will see a difference.” Derek: “So it’s not going to be even worse picture.” MM: “No it can’t be, it can’t be worse I guarantee you.” But will money be spent on delivering services? Some say not, as it was reported the municipality spent R300,000 on a mayoral public relations event. Derek: “I see a conflict between the skulls, bones fences at Komani and spending on thousands at a mayoral address, apparently R300,000?” Mayor: “Whatever figure that you might put, but for us to bring back the trust of the community, but also to make them understand what the government is doing for them, especially this fee of government, you have to spend money.” Rental car mayor Derek: “It was reported that you are driving a rental car which is costing R78,000 a month, is that true?” Mayor: “That is for one reason, is that the car driven by the former mayor is in repairs.” But the mayoral car has been in repairs for half a year. Rental car MM volvo pictures MM: “Let’s say yes, it comes to that amount.” Derek: “But that is just incredible? I don’t know what you spend R78,000 on. It’s a Volvo?” MM: “Unless you’re saying we were given a raw deal?” Fried Chicken MM Derek: “On your list of priorities is it more important to spend R90,000 on fried chicken or money on cleaning up the townships.” MM: “The priorities of this mun has been sent is the roads, electricity, cleanliness of the city.” Derek: “But you haven’t answered the question.” MM: “If you compare to what we spend to cleaning up the towns and township each month, that R90,000 is far less.” Derek: “Madam mayor at Carte Blanche we are used to people making promises.” Mayor: “Please do come back in 6 months. The future is very bright for this municipality.” One certainty is that the stench of maladministration across many of South Africa’s municipality’s needs to be cleaned up – just like Komani’s streets. 10 seconds: Upsound: “Auctioneer: Going once for R250,000, going twice…” Why was an Eastern Cape municipality forced to auction off some of its most vital service delivery assets? 15 seconds: Fried chicken for R90,000 and a rental car for R78,000 monthly, will new management at an Eastern Cape municipality be able to save it from itself? Mayor: “It’s very bad, it’s very pathetic.” 15 seconds: Upsound: “Auctioneer: Going once...” After auctioning off a fire brigade, road graders and garbage collection vehicles, can Queenstown’s municipality continue to deliver basic services? MM: “It can’t be worse I guarantee you.” 30 seconds: MM: If you compare to what we spend to cleaning up the towns and township each month, that R90,000 is far less than what we spent. Queenstown’s municipality in the Eastern Cape is in a financial crisis and unable to provide basic services. Residents are fed-up but despite this - financial mismanagement is still rife Derek: “But that is just incredible? I don’t know what you spend R78,000 on.”

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Queenstown municipality has auctioned off it's vehicles to pay for a historical debt, but the municipality is in tatters, and there is no water, electricity of service delivery.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: GOING, GOING, GONE: Various municipal vehicles, most of which are imperative for service deliverywere sold today at an auction to recover millions of rands owed by the Enoch Mgijima Local Municipalityto Milowo Trading Enterprise. Robert Goss of Milowo Trading Enterprise said he and his legal representatives would soon file for municipal buildings to be sold as well. The debt owed to Milowo trading, following the building of a community hall in Sterkstroom in 2012, and accumulated interest, has been set at R58-million. Vehicles that went under the hammer included 18 trucks, various traffic vehicles and a grader. The full story will be in The Rep next week Picture: ANDISA BONANI It was decided that the town would go under section 123 (That’s under administration) – but they haven’t decided whether that’s division a,b,c yet. However, they still might go under section 125, because they are saying that treasury’s R100 million was not enough to assist them during the amalgamation. (The municipality amalgamated late last year – from 3 to 1). But it needs to be properly approved. Then they are going to have a SECOND auction because they didn’t make enough on the first, but they want to have a meeting about it before – it’s meant to go ahead on July 29th. Their current Mayor and Municipal Manager were only appointed in February. The manager was embroiled in the 600 million toilet Mandela scandal, and there are rumours about the Mayors BMW. We will do a full audit on both of them and their families, the community know a lot about where they live etc.
